summary.text: A 68-year-old woman with hypertension and diabetes mellitus reportedly had a cerebrovascular event of undocumented subtype about five years before presentation, leaving right-sided hemiparesis. Recurrent focal motor seizures evolving to bilateral tonic-clonic seizures began about two years later, increasing from 1-2 to 3-4 per year, with a recent flurry and new right-sided epilepsia partialis continua.

Neurological consultation initially yielded a diagnosis of post-stroke epilepsy with suspected new structural or metabolic insult. Metabolic panel and blood count were essentially normal. EEG showed left hemispheric slowing, left lateralized periodic discharges and left mid-temporal epileptiform discharges. Brain MRI showed left unihemispheric cerebral atrophy with ex-vacuo ventricular dilatation and no significant contrast enhancement.

Adult-onset Rasmussen encephalitis was strongly suggested, the earlier attribution to the cerebrovascular event was considered unlikely, and metabolic causes were excluded. The patient and relatives were counselled; immunosuppressive or surgical options were not pursued, and management focused on seizure control and quality of life.

Her existing levetiracetam and sodium valproate regimen was up titrated, resulting in significant reduction in seizure frequency while she awaited consent to proceed with further diagnostic and therapeutic interventions. She was scheduled for follow-up and supportive rehabilitation.
